{{Short description|Species of flowering plant}} {{Use dmy dates|date=July 2019}} {{Speciesbox |image = Arthropodium VUW.jpg |taxon = Arthropodium cirratum |authority = ([[G.Forst.]]) [[R.Br.]] |synonyms = ''Anthericum cirratum'' G.Forst.
''Anthericum latifolium'' [[Joseph Banks|Banks]] & [[Sol.]] ex [[Carl Sigismund Kunth|Kunth]] |synonyms_ref = }} '''''Arthropodium cirratum''''' commonly known as '''rengarenga''', '''renga lily''', '''New Zealand rock lily''', or '''maikaika''', is a species of [[herbaceous]] [[perennial plant]], [[endemic (ecology)|endemic]] to New Zealand, where it may once have been farmed. It is used for medicine as well as food, and has symbolic importance in traditional [[Māori culture]]. The [[Māori language|Māori]] name ''rengarenga'' is a reduplication of [[Proto-Polynesian language|Proto-Polynesian]] *''renga'' which in other related languages corresponds to [[turmeric]], especially its powdered form (see {{langx|sm|lega}}, {{langx|haw|lena}}); this association is due to both plants' similar stem and root characteristics.{{cite web|url=http://www.temarareo.org/TMR-Rengarenga.html |title=Rengarenga|date=2022|access-date=30 October 2022|website=Te Māra Reo|publisher=Benson Family Trust}} == Description == The [[Leaf|leaves]] are {{Convert|30-60|cm|abbr = on}} long and {{Convert|3-10|cm|abbr = on}} wide.{{Cite book |last=Lehnebach |first=Carlos A. |url=https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q115065494 |title=Native Plants of Aotearoa |last2=Meudt |first2=Heidi |date=2022-10-01 |publisher=Te Papa Press |isbn=978-1-9911509-3-6 |series=Te Papa Te Taiao Nature Series |pages=23 |language=English}} The [[Peduncle (botany)|flower stalk]] often reaches one metre, and bears many white six-petalled [[flower]]s, in groups of two or three, each about {{Convert|2|cm|4=1|abbr=on}} across. The [[stamen]]s are tricoloured - purple and white, with yellow at the curled end. The roots are {{Convert|2-3|cm|1|abbr=on}} wide. [[File:Rengarenga flower (Arthropodium cirrhatum).jpg|thumb|upright|Rengarenga flower]] [[File:Renga Renga Leaves 2.JPG|thumb|right|Rengarenga leaves]] ==Taxonomy== It was first described in 1786 as ''Anthericum cirrhatum'' by [[Georg Forster]]. In 1822, [[Robert Brown (botanist, born 1773)|Robert Brown]] assigned it to the genus, ''Arthropodium'', resulting in the name, ''Arthropodium cirrhatum (''now ''A. cirratum.)'' == Distribution and habitat == It occurs naturally north of [[Greymouth]] and [[Kaikōura]] near the sea and, as the name suggests, usually on rocks. ==Cultivation and uses== It is often grown as an [[Ornamental plant|ornamental]] plant. The [[rhizome]]s are edible when cooked and can be found throughout the year. The rhizomes were once eaten by the [[Māori people|Māori]] after being cooked in a [[hāngī]]. [[William Colenso]] believed, for two reasons, that this plant was once cultivated by them: firstly, the plant grows much larger under cultivation than it usually does in the wild; and secondly it was often found near old deserted Māori homes and plantations. However, he lists it as only fourteenth in importance, in his list of eighteen kinds of wild vegetable food used by the [[Māori people|Māori]]. ==References== {{Reflist|refs= {{Cite web|url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:530468-1|title=Anthericum latifolium Banks & Sol. ex Kunth. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science|website=Plants of the World Online|access-date=2019-11-24}} {{cite book|author=Crowe, A. |title=A Field Guide to the Native Edible Plants of New Zealand|year= 2004|publisher=Penguin Books.
